payload.name: Extract encouragement after setbacks
payload.description: When a speaker offers encouragement, reassurance, or advice to persist after a listener's setback or failure, during extraction and CRUD.
content: When a speaker responds to a listener's setback with explicit encouragement, reassurance, or advice to persist, capture the core gist as a candidate memory that records the speaker, listener, and the substance of the encouragement (e.g., rejections don't define you, keep trying, you'll find the right opportunity).
During CRUD, if no memory of that encouragement exists, create it as a relationship or event memory; if a partial version exists, update it with the missing outlook or advice.
Stop after the core encouragement; do not extract generic pleasantries, greetings, or unsupported factual claims.

candidates.solves: Extraction skips expressive support statements (encouragement, reassurance, advice after a setback) because they are not objective facts, losing what one person told another. Apply when a speaker explicitly responds to a listener's setback with reassurance, persistence advice, or positive outlook; extract the gist as a relationship/event memory and create it if absent. Do not apply to factual claims, greetings, or filler.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Motivation Statements
payload.description: When a message explicitly states the reason or motivation behind a behavior, commitment, or ongoing activity (e.g., 'what keeps me going', 'motivates me', 'I keep doing X because'), use that stated reason as the core of the extracted or updated memory content rather than only the surrounding feelings.
content: During extraction, when a message contains an explicit motivational or causal statement such as '...is what keeps me going', '...motivates me', or 'I keep doing X because...', capture the stated reason as an explicit clause or separate claim in the candidate; do not replace it with only emotional or evaluative paraphrases.
During CRUD updates, when enriching or merging an existing memory, carry forward any explicitly stated motivation from the source message; prune only redundant detail, not the stated reason itself.
Apply only to motivations explicitly stated by the speaker; do not infer hidden motives, and stop once the stated reason is captured.

candidates.solves: Users often state why they persist or value something explicitly; extraction may paraphrase the emotional context and drop the stated reason, so the memory never holds the fact needed to answer later 'what motivates X' questions. This Skill applies to future messages where a speaker explicitly states what motivates or keeps them going while creating or updating a memory. It must not apply when no stated reason exists and motivation would require inference.

payload.name: Extract idiomatic commitment statements
payload.description: When a speaker states their own intention or commitment using idiomatic or negated phrasing such as 'not giving up', 'won't stop', or 'keep going', extract a memory capturing the underlying action.
content: During extraction, treat statements where a person says they will or won't do something, including idiomatic or negated equivalents, as candidates for a 'state' or 'plan' memory (e.g., [person] intends to / not to [action]).

Resolve the idiomatic expression to its concrete action (e.g., 'not giving up' -> not quit) and link the memory to the source message. Only apply when the statement is a personal commitment about a future course of action.

candidates.solves: Extraction sometimes misses a person's stated commitment when it is phrased idiomatically or with negation (e.g., 'I'm not giving up'), so the fact is never stored. This skill applies when a speaker tells someone their own intended course of action using such indirect phrasing; extract it as a state/plan memory. It should not apply to direct explicit statements the base extractor already handles, nor to purely affective remarks with no concrete action.

No existing Skill covers preserving explicit motivation statements.
No existing Skill covers extracting idiomatic commitment statements.
